ontology_dependency.mapped_preflight_intent: independently assess the frozen conformance material
ontology_dependency.selected_dependency_result: exact successor freeze recomputed without drift

relation_evidence.claim_ceiling_observed: distinct local provider observations, not independent proof or external conformance

independent_execution.interpretation: The exact frozen workspace compiles and its enabled local tests pass. PostgreSQL and exact-SBF load evidence are supplied by the two-cycle stable receipt; no Devnet path was executed.

positive_observations: The content cipher is XChaCha20-Poly1305 with random 192-bit nonces and context AAD.
Owner envelopes use HPKE Base mode X25519/HKDF-SHA256/ChaCha20-Poly1305 with recipient and artifact context in AAD.
Generated and recovered content keys and file-loaded HPKE private bytes are wrapped in Zeroizing containers.
The PostgreSQL adapter uses separate operational, recovery and archive schemas; recovery and archive mutation triggers fail closed in the local conformance fixture.
The native program checks signers, program ownership, PDAs, revisions and replay-marker creation, and Solana transaction rollback preserves tested negative pre-state.
The terminal RPC is fixed to public Devnet and the expected genesis hash is checked before any Solana effect.

findings.title: The terminal gate does not authenticate an accepted binding or owner authorization
findings.evidence: accepted_binding_digest is checked only for hexadecimal shape and is never compared with accepted repository evidence. authorization_digest is accepted when a caller-controlled environment variable repeats the envelope value; packet digest equality protects bytes only if the launcher is already trusted.
findings.impact: A caller possessing external key material can manufacture an envelope and matching environment values. The binary cannot distinguish an owner-authorized packet from a self-asserted packet.
findings.required_disposition: Bind execution to a separately trusted owner-decision input and current accepted binding identity, or explicitly designate and enforce a trusted launcher boundary that supplies non-self-assertable authorization.

findings.title: The 192-transaction deployment budget is a candidate scope expansion and is not measured or enforced
findings.evidence: The exact 93,296-byte SBF requires at least 76 packet-sized submissions and has a conservative local bound of 185. The original 24-total cap is impossible. The new gate accepts 192 deployment submissions plus 24 protocol submissions, but deployment is delegated to the CLI and only --max-sign-attempts 1 is passed; actual deployment submissions are neither counted nor emitted.
findings.impact: The successor cannot operate under the original envelope, and the replacement envelope can exceed its deployment submission ceiling without runtime detection.
findings.required_disposition: Obtain a terminal owner decision for the split scope and enforce or independently attest the actual deployment transaction count before treating the 192 bound as closed.

findings.title: Successful deployment does not prove the executable account contains the exact frozen SBF
findings.evidence: The executor verifies local SBF and caller-declared CLI hashes, invokes program deploy, then checks only that the selected program account is executable. It does not pin the CLI hash to the frozen Agave identity, inspect loader/programdata authority, dump deployed bytes, compare remote program data with the frozen SBF, or record deployment signatures and slots.
findings.impact: A successful CLI result and executable account are insufficient evidence that the exact frozen bytes were deployed once with the intended authority posture.
findings.required_disposition: Pin the deployment tool identity, establish fresh/existing program and upgrade-authority posture, record deployment transactions, and independently verify the finalized deployed program bytes or an authoritative byte-equivalent loader identity.

findings.title: HPKE and Solana identity coherence is checked only after irreversible Devnet effects
findings.evidence: Distinct paths are required, but equal key contents are not rejected. Public/private HPKE key correspondence is not tested in prepare_material. B decryption occurs after grant finalization; A private-key use occurs during rewrap after grant; B replacement-key decryption occurs after reissue fulfillment. Wallet keypairs are not checked for pairwise distinct public keys.
findings.impact: Mismatched or aliased external inputs can leave a deployed program, initialized artifact, granted B, or fulfilled reissue on Devnet before the executor discovers the error and stops.
findings.required_disposition: Before deployment, prove A/B/B2 public-private correspondence, perform prepare/open/rewrap/open locally, and enforce pairwise-distinct wallet and HPKE identities.

findings.title: The requested replacement key is not cryptographically bound to the fulfilled envelope
findings.evidence: ProductionCryptography::rewrap_for_reissue accepts a replacement public key argument without verifying it against the replacement binding fingerprint or immutable key-directory record. The Solana request stores replacement_key_commitment, while fulfillment accepts an independent replacement_envelope_commitment and only returns the key commitment as return data.
findings.impact: An originator or faulty caller can fulfill B's request with an envelope for a different key while on-chain revision and fulfilled state advance successfully.
findings.required_disposition: Define one exact key-envelope binding commitment, validate it in the crypto adapter, and preserve/enforce it through request and fulfillment state.

findings.title: Recipient and replacement decryption use in-memory material rather than post-finality durable retrieval
findings.evidence: Ciphertext and envelopes are persisted and immediately verified in three layers, but after finalized grant and reissue the executor opens material retained in PreparedTrial. It never reconstructs PreparedMaterial from SQL locators after finality or a restart.
findings.impact: The Devnet vertical would not demonstrate the required storage-to-finalized-chain-to-recipient recovery path, and durable envelope availability after process loss remains unproven.
findings.required_disposition: After finalized observations, retrieve ciphertext and the active recipient envelope through recorded locators, verify identities, reconstruct material, and decrypt those retrieved bytes; include restart evidence in the terminal trial if required by the obligation.

findings.title: The public artifact identifier is an unsalted SHA-256 digest of plaintext
findings.evidence: prepare_material sets both artifact_version_id and plaintext_commitment to SHA-256(plaintext), and artifact_version_id is placed in public program state and PDA seeds.
findings.impact: Low-entropy definitions or known candidate knowledge can be confirmed by offline guessing, leaking equality and content membership despite ciphertext confidentiality.
findings.required_disposition: Adopt the explicitly governed confidentiality posture: use a domain-separated hiding commitment with adequate random salt or declare deterministic plaintext-commitment leakage as an accepted product threat boundary.

findings.title: The terminal receipt cannot support the enumerated cases and cost observations at the required granularity
findings.evidence: The envelope requires 15 case IDs, but TrialEvidence.cases records only submitted protocol transactions. Storage readiness, finalized fetch, both decryptions, state isolation and cost observation are summarized fields rather than distinct case records. Deployment and airdrop signatures/slots/fees are absent, rent is not separated, and storage cost is a fixed string.
findings.impact: A PASS_BOUNDED_DEVNET result would still lack the exact per-case and infrastructure-cost evidence needed by the terminal plan.
findings.required_disposition: Emit one record for every enumerated case, deployment and airdrop evidence, actual protocol/deployment fees and rent, storage observations, and exact input/output identities.

findings.title: An RPC or finality timeout can leave an effect without a durable partial receipt
findings.evidence: Submission uses max_retries 0 and stops on errors, but a send error or the 120-second finality timeout can occur after network acceptance. Trial evidence is written only after complete success, and deployment CLI failures also produce no structured partial-effect or reconciliation receipt.
findings.impact: The required stop-on-first-failure behavior is present, but the resulting external state can be ambiguous and unauditable.
findings.required_disposition: Persist an external append-only attempt journal before each effect and record signature/program identity immediately, then reconcile finalized state without resubmission after ambiguous outcomes.

findings.title: The trial accepts an arbitrary PostgreSQL URL while SQLx is built with tls-none
findings.evidence: KEP_POSTGRES_TRIAL_URL is not restricted to a loopback/local provider and the adapter enables tls-none. Database credentials remain outside the repository and stored bytes are encrypted, but a remote URL could expose credentials and metadata on an unprotected transport.
findings.impact: The local-first trial assumption is not enforced by the executor.
findings.required_disposition: Require loopback/local PostgreSQL for this binding or add a pinned authenticated TLS posture for remote providers.

findings.title: Concurrent first recovery events can fork the hash-linked journal
findings.evidence: append_recovery locks the most recent row, but an empty journal has no row to lock; concurrent initial writers can both use the all-zero predecessor.
findings.impact: Append-only mutation protection remains intact, but a global single-chain claim is not established under concurrent initialization.
findings.required_disposition: Serialize journal appends with an advisory/table lock or a singleton head row and add a concurrent-writer test.

findings.title: The public program accepts zero commitments and a default recipient key
findings.evidence: Only epoch zero is rejected at initialization. Artifact, policy, ciphertext, envelope, locator, operation and replacement commitments are raw arrays without nonzero validation; grant rejects recipient equal to A but not Pubkey::default().
findings.impact: Malformed states can satisfy instruction success while carrying no meaningful commitment or usable B identity.
findings.required_disposition: Reject null commitment values and invalid recipient identities where the admitted model requires qualified nonzero identities.

findings.title: Byte zeroization is partial and filesystem custody policy is external
findings.evidence: HPKE private file bytes, plaintext and content keys use Zeroizing, but the executor does not enforce file permissions, encrypted-at-rest key custody, memory locking, or explicit zeroization guarantees for loaded Solana Keypair values and HPKE provider internals.
findings.impact: The implementation is suitable only for disposable local trial secrets under a trusted host, not production custody.
findings.required_disposition: Keep the claim bounded to disposable Devnet keys and define a production custody adapter and host controls before any stronger security claim.

findings.title: Lockfile pinning is present but vulnerability and license assessment evidence is absent
findings.evidence: Relevant RustCrypto, SQLx and Solana versions and registry checksums are locked. The reviewed packet contains no advisory scan, deny policy, SBOM, provenance attestation, or license review.
findings.impact: Exact dependency identity is known, but known-vulnerability and policy posture is not.
findings.required_disposition: Run a current advisory and dependency policy assessment against the frozen lockfile and preserve the result as bounded evidence.

findings.title: The terminal orchestration has no local mock or fault-injection coverage
findings.evidence: The trial crate's two tests cover only budget-envelope arithmetic. execute, path boundaries, trusted gate inputs, deployment command construction, submission accounting, partial failures and evidence serialization are compiled but not exercised locally.
findings.impact: Program-test and adapter tests do not validate the terminal coordinator's cross-layer failure behavior.
findings.required_disposition: Factor RPC/deployment/storage/custody ports and add deterministic coordinator tests for every enumerated success, rejection and ambiguous-failure path before Devnet authorization.

findings.title: Formal provider passes prove abstract models, not preservation into Rust, SQL or Solana bytes
findings.evidence: Lean, TLC and Alloy outputs are deterministic PASS_BOUNDED projections. Their receipts explicitly deny runtime and external conformance; several propositions are satisfied by model definitions rather than a machine-checked refinement from implementation.
findings.impact: The formal evidence is useful bounded model evidence but cannot discharge implementation conformance findings.
findings.required_disposition: Preserve the existing claim ceiling and add a separately reviewed refinement/preservation layer if formal-to-code conformance is required.

split_budget_assessment.runtime_enforcement_result: not_evaluable-as-closed because actual CLI deployment submissions are not counted or independently attested

review_summary.positive_evidence_result: Local deterministic tests, crypto vectors, PostgreSQL conformance, native program-test, exact SBF load, formal bounded providers and 204 relation records are present and current, but they do not resolve the findings above.

residues: Souffle remains deferred because the admitted obligations do not require a closed-world recursive query.
No real Devnet observation, transaction signature, finalized slot, rent record or recipient retrieval evidence exists in this review.
The split deployment/protocol budget is a candidate terminal decision, not inherited authority.
Mainnet readiness, production security, availability, publication, release and deployment authority remain outside scope.
claim_ceiling: Independent review of exact frozen local material only. This receipt does not accept a binding, authorize Devnet, establish conformance, approve publication, or grant deployment authority.
